prize_parts.citation: For developing the political-economy theory of trade policy, showing how lobbying and organised interests shape trade protection.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part on B001 for Helpman and Grossman. I have narrowed the citation to the political economy of trade protection, which is the discovery the ballot states. The protection-for-sale framework made lobbying and tariff formation an equilibrium object with testable implications, and it has been extended, estimated and used in the analysis of trade agreements for about three decades. Attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: a long, tightly coupled two-person partnership, with the 1994 paper and the book on interest groups and trade policy as central outputs. A two-name citation therefore needs no arbitrary exclusion. The contribution also connects trade theory to the study of political institutions, which gives it reach beyond one subfield. I now rest the case only on attribution, maturity and durable conceptual influence. Round 1 agreement among members is not evidence of merit and I do not count it. The chair summary asks whether the growth strand belongs in the citation. I say no. The strand is real joint work, but the ballot does not define it as the discovery, and including it would invite the overlap questions with 2008 and 2025 that members raised and that this simulation has not verified.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains empirical. Structural estimates of the protection-for-sale equilibrium are sensitive to specification and support for its functional forms is mixed. Part of the contribution is therefore a disciplined framework and research programme, not a settled quantitative result, and a citation must not overclaim. A second reservation is distinctness. Krugman's 2008 prize concerned adjacent trade theory, and the 2025 prize recognised innovation-driven growth. These points come from the members' files and I have not checked them independently. A third is Helpman's separate credit on B030. I treat it as a different achievement, but a committee wishing to honour trade through firm heterogeneity could reasonably prefer that line. I am also the chair and one of the B001 supporters, so I should be careful not to let my process role favour my own position.

responses.point: Krusell finds the mixed protection-for-sale record more worrying than the other supporters do. He suggests the lasting value is as an organising theory, whereas BLP has been validated by three decades of use. He calls B001 a close alternative and says the two cases differ in kind (framework versus method) and not in strength. He also warns against widening the B001 citation to endogenous growth.
responses.response: I agree on the citation: I have confined it to political economy and removed any reference to growth. I accept that the empirical record is the real question, and I would not call the functional forms confirmed. My view is that an organising theory that made lobbying measurable, and so produced a large literature that tests, qualifies and sometimes contradicts it, is a prize-sized contribution. That differs from a framework that was never testable. I also take his point that BLP has a stronger record of validated use. What keeps B002 behind B001 for me is not the method-versus-discovery distinction. It is the credit structure: seven names under a three-name cap, with Bresnahan and Reiss excluded and Pakes's dynamic-games work partly separate. Our disagreement is on weighting, and it is narrower than the ballot ranks suggest.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson moved from Katz to Dorn, confined the B018 citation to technology and trade shocks to labour demand, and treats the open shift-share and persistence debates as evidence of maturity. She notes that the 2024 prize concerned institutions and prosperity, so it did not cover the task framework.
responses.response: I concede the Acemoglu point. In round 1 I treated the 2024 prize as relevant to the task-framework credit, and her reading of that prize as about institutions and prosperity is the better one. I withdraw that part of my reservation. Her move to Autor, Dorn and Hanson, with a citation limited to the trade-shock and labour-demand evidence, also makes the three-name set more stable, which answers the chair's question. That is why B018 replaces B036 among my alternatives. I still keep it behind B001. The China-shock evidence dates from about 2013, and the long-run size and persistence of the effects are still being re-estimated. I read that as a productive debate, but it argues for more consolidation time than a framework used for three decades requires. I would not call that a weakness of the work.

responses.point: Dreber prefers B030 because firm heterogeneity and selection have been confronted with micro data more densely than protection-for-sale. She names the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as the main weakness, and says Helpman's two credits are different contributions by one person that should be compared on how well established and cleanly attributed each is.
responses.response: I agree with her rule for handling Helpman's two credits: compare the contributions on how well established and cleanly attributed each is, and do not combine them or count one against the other. By that rule I concede that B030 has been tested more densely against micro data. B001 is clearer on attribution, because B030 has a gap she herself calls real and that cannot be closed within a three-name citation without weakening the Melitz-Helpman core. Whether denser testing outweighs cleaner credit is a judgement of weighting. I would not call B030 a weaker scientific contribution. A Grossman-Helpman award does not preclude later recognition of the firm-level strand.

responses.point: Teorell supports B001 with a broader citation that leads with organised interests and trade policy and also names the integration of innovation and growth into trade theory. He treats the growth strand as supporting, and says the 2025 overlap should be confirmed by the committee since he has not verified it.
responses.response: I agree with his priority of putting political economy first. I would go one step further and drop the growth clause. He has not verified the 2025 overlap and neither have I, and a clause whose standing we cannot check would be a risk in the citation. Naming it as supporting would still make it part of what the prize rewards. The two-name credit does not depend on it, because the Grossman-Helpman partnership is documented through the protection-for-sale papers and the book. If the committee wants the broader pairing, that should be an explicit decision with an argument for what the growth strand adds. It should not be added by implication.

uncertainties: How much weight the mixed, specification-sensitive empirical record of protection-for-sale should carry against its role in organising theory and empirical work.
Whether the narrow political-economy citation is distinct enough from Krugman's 2008 prize and from the 2025 growth prize. I have relied on members' descriptions of both and have not verified them.
Whether the committee will treat Helpman's credit on B001 and B030 as separate achievements, as I do, or as competing framings of a trade prize.
Whether the B018 Autor-Dorn-Hanson set and its persistence evidence will have consolidated enough to outweigh B001's attribution advantage in a later year.
My assessments rest on general knowledge and colleagues' stated facts, not independently verified citation or impact data.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for the preferred laureates, Helpman and Grossman. My listed frequent co-authors (Krusell, Olovsson, Storesletten, Zilibotti, Rodríguez Mora) and committee co-authors (Boppart, Friberg) are not credited on B001. I am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart, and Krusell is the committee secretary and a B002 supporter. For disclosure on alternatives, B050 (Moore, Gertler, Kiyotaki, Gilchrist) and B018 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Katz) list no names among my documented co-authors. I have dropped B036 from my alternatives. My opening noted a possible institutional link to Persson at IIES, which my profile does not document. I disclose it without adjudicating it. I am the chair and one of the B001 supporters, and I flag that role so that this statement is not read as a ruling. I have not independently verified any source or claim about confidential proceedings.
